new_task_1.title: Allow method-preserving routing redirects in debug mode
new_task_1.description: Flask 2.1.0 stops treating 307 and 308 routing redirects as debug-time form-data errors. In debug mode, Flask should only replace a routing redirect with `FormDataRoutingRedirect` when the redirect status would cause the client to drop the original method or request body.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Flask 2.1.0 does not raise the debug-only `FormDataRoutingRedirect` assertion for routing redirects that use HTTP 307 or 308, since those status codes preserve the request method and body.

expectation.grounded: In `Flask.raise_routing_exception`, debug-mode interception of `RequestRedirect` should skip redirects whose status code is 307 or 308. Flask should continue re-raising the original routing redirect for those codes, while still converting other non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS routing redirects into `FormDataRoutingRedirect` when the redirect could discard request data.
expectation.conceptual: Debug mode should only block routing redirects that are actually unsafe for form submissions. Method-preserving redirects should behave like normal routing redirects instead of being treated as data-loss errors.

constraints.grounded: Do not change non-debug routing behavior. Do not stop raising `FormDataRoutingRedirect` for non-safe redirect cases that still use redirect statuses other than 307 or 308 on non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests. The change is limited to recognizing that 307 and 308 preserve the original request semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should narrow an over-eager debug safeguard without removing the safeguard entirely. Unsafe redirects should still be surfaced clearly in debug mode.

behavior: In debug mode, a routing redirect with status 307 is re-raised as the original redirect instead of being replaced by `FormDataRoutingRedirect`.
In debug mode, a routing redirect with status 308 is re-raised as the original redirect instead of being replaced by `FormDataRoutingRedirect`.
In debug mode, non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS routing redirects that use redirect statuses other than 307 or 308 still raise `FormDataRoutingRedirect`.
When `FormDataRoutingRedirect` is raised, its message explains that the problem applies to redirects that would cause the browser to drop the method or body.
acceptance_criteria: When a non-GET request triggers a routing redirect with HTTP 307 while Flask is in debug mode, Flask should propagate the original redirect behavior rather than raising `FormDataRoutingRedirect`.
When a non-GET request triggers a routing redirect with HTTP 308 while Flask is in debug mode, Flask should propagate the original redirect behavior rather than raising `FormDataRoutingRedirect`.
When a non-GET request triggers a routing redirect with a status that does not preserve the request body, Flask should still raise `FormDataRoutingRedirect` in debug mode.

When the debug-only assertion is raised, the error text should describe that browsers drop form data for non-307/308 routing redirects and direct the request toward the canonical URL or a method-preserving redirect.
